Nos Elyzabet filia quondam nobilis viri Bopponis comitis de Wertheym, rclicta quondam Gotfridi domini de Uohenloch, omnibus presentes literas inspecturis salutem in eo a quo omnis sapiencia derivatur. Quia juxta psalmistam, nisi dominus edificaverit domum, in vanum labo- rant, qui edificant: licet igitur dudum sollicite et interne ante retroacta tempora cogitare ceperimus ac devotis me- ditationibus diebus et noctibus involverimus mentem nostram, quomodo et qualiter regi regum domino de suis donis et he— neficiis nobis per eum impensis redderemus ad sui honoris gloriam et famulatus augmentum aliqualem recompensam, de- mum ex largiflua bonitate ipsius, sine qua nullum bonum concipitur et frequenti meditatione concepimus et in hoc fir— mavimus anchoram nostri cordis, quod felices essemus, si hujusmodi nostra sollicitudine expensisque ac oportunis labo- ribus humilem ordinem ac sanctam religionem fratrum Car- thusiens. quorum vita est exemplar vite et conversationis domini nostri Jesu Christi, dum in terris deguit humani ge- Wcrthein. tlrkundrnhui-h. r 82 neris pro salute ac sui precursoris clamantis in deserto, ad partes Franconie et Mogoni, ubi dictus ordo est incognitus, deducere valeremus. Quesita sic et inyenta oportunitate ut speramus dictis fratribus prope civitatem Mogunt. habitantibus nomine ipsorum et totius ordinis infrascripta bona juxta alveum Mogoni apud oppidum Wert heim dedimus, donavi- mus et damus in hiis scriptis. Et omiie jus et actionem no- bis competens in ipsis bonis directe vel indirecte in presenti vel in luturo, in dictos fratres et eorum ordinem transferi- mus per presentes, pure, simpliciter et in totum pro remedio animarum patris, matris, nostrorum progenitorum et consan- guineorum et nostrarum ac omnium et singulorum, qui ad hujusmodi donationem et translationem fideliter dederint au- xiiium, consilium vel favorem pro monasterio et conventu infra terminos dictorum bonorum in loco magis apto, qui ipsis placuerit construendo et deo perpetuo famulando, ut populus dei eorum sanctis eruditis exemplis in sue devotionis proficiat salubriter incrementis. Quam donationem et trans- lationem in vero verbo et bona fide promittimus ratam, gratam et firmam perpetue in omnibus tenere et etiam observare nee contravenire vel volenti consentire, verbo vel facto publice vel occulte, renunciantes libere, ex certa scientia omni so- lempnitate, si qua fieri consuevit vel deberet in donationibus vel Iranslationibus faciendis ac alio omni juris sufiragio ca nonici et civilis, per quod premissa vitiari possent, seu quo- modolibet impugnari. entries.english:
LXXIV. Elisabeth von Hohenlohe, née Countess of Wertheim, founds the Charterhouse of Grünau by a deed of gift. 16 March 1328.

“In the name of the Lord, amen. We, Elyzabet, daughter of the late noble Boppo, Count of Wertheim, and widow of the late Gotfrid, Lord of Hohenlohe, greet all who see this letter in Him from whom all wisdom flows. The Psalmist says, ‘Unless the Lord builds the house, those who build it labor in vain.’ For a long time we have diligently and inwardly considered, in devout meditation day and night, how we might make some return to the King of kings for His gifts and benefits, granted to us for His glory and the increase of His service. At last, through His abundant goodness, without which no good can be conceived, and by much reflection, we conceived this purpose and fixed our hearts upon it: we would be happy if, through our care, expense, and suitable labor, we could bring the humble order and holy religion of the Carthusian brothers—whose life is an example of the life and conduct of our Lord Jesus Christ when He dwelt on earth for the salvation of humankind, and of His forerunner crying in the wilderness—to Franconia and the region of the Main, where that order is unknown.

“Having sought and, as we hope, found a suitable opportunity, we give, have given, and by this deed donate, in the name of those brothers living near Mainz and of their entire order, the following properties beside the Main near the town of Wertheim. We transfer to those brothers and their order all right and claim we have in these properties, directly or indirectly, now or in the future, purely, simply, and wholly, for the salvation of the souls of our father, mother, ancestors, kin, ourselves, and everyone who faithfully gives aid, counsel, or support to this donation and transfer. The purpose is to build a monastery and convent within the boundaries of the said properties, at the place they prefer, and to serve God there perpetually, so that God’s people may grow in devotion through their holy and learned example.

“We promise in truth and good faith that this gift and transfer shall forever remain valid, approved, and firm in every respect, and that we shall observe it and neither act against it nor consent to anyone doing so, openly or secretly, by word or deed. We freely and knowingly waive every formality customarily required or that ought to be required for gifts or transfers, and every other remedy of canon or civil law by which the foregoing might be invalidated or challenged. For greater certainty, we voluntarily agree that if we act contrary to any part of this deed as stated above, the honorable judges of the Holy See of Mainz and the official of the Würzburg court, or either of them without requiring the other, may pronounce sentence of excommunication against us until we make due satisfaction, without further judicial proceedings.

“The properties are: our village of Schalbrunnen, with its district, boundary, people, meadows, pastures, fields, vineyards, waters, streams, woods, rights, jurisdictions, rents, revenues, spiritual and temporal assets, corporeal and incorporeal assets, and all other appurtenances and dependencies, whatever they may be called. Also two mills called ‘Yringes Mit ien,’ situated above the bank called ‘dye Hascia,’ upstream from Schalbrunnen. Also six acres of vines on the right-hand side when traveling from the Wertheim Cross toward Haselach, on the hill called ‘der Bylsteyn.’ Also, in the village of Altavil, twenty malters of rye and two malters of oats, reckoning two malters of oats as one malter of rye, payable by the feasts of St Michael and St Martin; and seven pounds of Hall pennies in annual rent there, payable every year on the Feast of St Martin, which we shall point out in person from our property if and when necessary. In witness of all these matters, our seal is attached to this deed. Done and issued in the year of the Lord 1328, on the Tuesday after the Sunday on which Laetare is sung.”

research: The printed heading gives 16 March 1328; the charter dates itself Tuesday after Laetare, which falls on 15 March in the Julian calendar.
